title: Gatebraid metrics file (gatebraid/metrics@1)
description: The metrics-file format fixed by protocols/convergence-metrics-v2.md §5 and frozen at M3 batch N1 with the other two shared interfaces (M3-PLAN.md §2 N1) — '§5: no generator defines its own output contract'. Until this freeze, values collect in working records only and no criterion consumes them; §3's readings and §7's admission gate all post-date it. One file records one scope for one subject. Gate-exit-scoped files are committed beside the gate record in the slice's evidence directory and NEVER inside the gate record itself (§5). The metric vocabulary is an ENUM per scope, not a free string, for the same reason the format is fixed at all: a free name field would let each generator define its own contract in the one place the contract lives.

scope.description: §5's four collection loci. The scope decides which metric names are admissible, which subject identifiers are required, and when the file is written.

subject.description: What this file measures. Required identifiers are enforced per scope below: a metrics file that cannot name its subject cannot be aggregated by citation (§4's one-source clause), and closure criteria consume committed, cited values.

gate_exit_ordinal.description: Which attempt at this gate exit this file records. The base unit is the gate exit ATTEMPTED (§1), so a second attempt is a second unit, not an overwrite.

recorded_at.description: The unit's own event time — gate exit, stop, batch close, terminal disposition. NEVER retrospective: §5's recording-time rule exists because a classification assigned later is assigned with knowledge the moment did not have.

finalized.description: Slice-scoped ONLY, and required there — both directions enforced below. protocols/convergence-metrics-v2.md §5 (Slice-scoped) is the single home of the rule: the authoritative committed home is finalized at Gate 3 exit or at an operator-authored terminal disposition, and GitHub Issue closure is never the finalization event. ADR-0025 §3 carries the terminal-disposition half as alignment.

event.description: Exactly two. 'issue-closure' is deliberately absent and is not an oversight.

reference.description: The control-plane object that IS the finalization: the Gate 3 record, or the operator's disposition comment id.

allOf.$comment: §5: a slice-scoped file's whole purpose is to be the committed value a closure criterion reads, so it must say which event finalized it — and must name its slice.
A gate-exit file must name the gate exit it belongs to, down to which attempt.
§5: batch-scoped metrics are recorded at batch close, slice or no slice.
§5: milestone-scoped metrics are computed at closure from the committed series, never from memory or narrative.

metricEntry.description: One metric reading. The three result states are structurally separated below, which is the whole point of this schema: §5 requires no_eligible_unit_ran, undefined_zero_denominator and numeric zero to be DISTINCT AND NAMED, and the M2 instrument's failures were exactly the class where a zero meant three different things.

entry_id.description: Stable identifier for this reading, unique within its file. It exists so that §5's correction rule — a correction is a superseding entry CITING the original, never a silent edit — can actually be obeyed: without an id there is nothing for a later entry to cite.

name.description: The metric's §5 name, constrained to the admissible enum for this file's scope by the conditionals above. A name outside its scope's set — a milestone metric in a gate-exit file, say — is rejected.

state.description: §5's three result states, never conflated. measured: units ran and a value exists — a numerator of genuinely zero is a REAL MEASUREMENT and is recorded here with value 0. no_eligible_unit_ran: the metric's unit never executed in the period; the metric does not move; it is NOT zero, and it carries no numerator or denominator because none was counted. undefined_zero_denominator: units ran but the denominator is empty; reported as undefined and NEVER as a number, and the empty denominator is recorded rather than implied.

value.description: Present if and only if state is measured. Number for a ratio or count; string for an interval (elapsed_calendar_time) or a reading (convergence_reading).

command.description: §4's honesty clause: a claimed value names the command that establishes it, and for a value counted from committed records, the counting command over those records. An unrun check is not evidence and a value nobody can recompute is decoration (ADR-0018 §2a).

observational.description: True for a series recorded but never used as a criterion — evidence_bytes_over_implementation_bytes is declared exactly this in §2. Marking it here stops a later reader from promoting an observation into a target.

alarm.description: contract_recurrence sets this. §3: recurrence is an IMMEDIATE ALARM — stop, adjudicate at the next stop point, record the ruling — and no longer a standing divergence verdict. Three unresolved alarms in a milestone escalate to a milestone-level review.

breakdown.description: Typed decomposition where §5 requires one. human_round_trips is typed by mechanism AND cause — the cause axis succeeds v1 §3.3's contract-caused-only counter, which had no category for M2's instrument-caused trips.

attribution.description: operator_attended_work_units only. §5: a batch serving no slice, or more than one, records its units as unattributed phase overhead — NEVER divided by formula among slices.

ladder_rung.description: instrument_defects_per_evidence_run only: the ADR-0028 ladder the defect sits on.

supersedes.description: §5's correction rule: a correction is a SUPERSEDING ENTRY citing the original, never a silent edit. Both fields are required because a corrected entry usually lives in an earlier committed file, so an id alone does not locate it.

file.description: Repository path of the file holding the superseded entry.

allOf.$comment: The core separation. A measured reading must carry a value and the command that establishes it; a non-measured state must NOT carry a value, which is what makes 'no unit ran' structurally unable to masquerade as zero.

§5: undefined_zero_denominator means units ran and the denominator is EMPTY. The denominator is required and must be zero — without the requirement the state is asserted and never shown, which is the same unevidenced-label class ADR-0028 §2 governs.
§5: no_eligible_unit_ran means the metric's unit NEVER EXECUTED. Carrying a numerator or denominator would be recording counts from units the state says did not run.
